We wanted embedded flows with one API user, but discovered that on page refresh, users could break out of the signing page and view/click around the entire account's data. DocuSign's fix required shifting to a legacy API version with no promise against sunsetting.

We paid $20,000 upfront after being told our use case would be supported, then got $0 back once we realized those promises weren't true. For a small startup, that felt like a crappy way to conduct business.
If you're trying to wrap an e-sign provider within your application, I would recommend HelloSign 1000x. HelloSign's API is a first class citizen whereas DocuSign's felt more like an afterthought.
We did exactly this embedded signing integration and it was fairly seamless - built a POC in Postman in about an hour and a Jr dev built a production service managing all our DocuSign integration.
We use the v2 REST API creating embedded envelope signing URLs without issues. Documentation is fantastic in its thoroughness - opposite experience of the failed integration described.
I once worked at a company that dealt with DocuSign integration; rumors were we paid more than double $20,000, and the integration never really took off, ending up a huge waste of money.

I received six DocuSign phishing emails, half using convincing subjects derived from actual DocuSign documents I had previously signed or processed, suggesting more than just email addresses were compromised.

At my work we've received dozens of phishing emails purportedly from DocuSign. Most are caught but some reach inboxes, which is dangerous since coworkers use DocuSign regularly and click links without suspicion.
As a real estate agent, DocuSign is used immensely, including with clients who are probably more susceptible to phishing scams following the email database breach.
